record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Analysis for Dirichlet Series
record.original_question: Does the Hardy space H^1 of Dirichlet series have a basis, and does it have an unconditional basis?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.6. Does H1 have a basis? Does it have an unconditional basis?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathscr{D}$ denote the algebra of formal Dirichlet series $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n n^{-s}$ with complex coefficients. For a Dirichlet polynomial $P(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{N} a_n n^{-s}$ define
$$\|P\|_{H^1} \;=\; \lim_{T\to\infty} \frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T} \left|\sum_{n=1}^{N} a_n n^{-it}\right|\,dt.$$
The Hardy space $H^1$ of Dirichlet series is the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials with respect to this norm; equivalently, via the Bohr lift $n^{-s}\mapsto z^{\kappa(n)}$ (where $\kappa(n)$ is the multi-index of prime exponents of $n$), $H^1$ is isometrically isomorphic to the Hardy space $H^1(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ of the infinite-dimensional polytorus.

A sequence $(e_k)_{k\ge 1}$ in a Banach space $X$ is a (Schauder) basis of $X$ if every $x\in X$ has a unique representation $x=\sum_{k=1}^\infty c_k(x) e_k$ with convergence in norm. The basis is unconditional if for every $x\in X$ this series converges unconditionally (i.e., for every permutation $\pi$ of $\mathbb{N}$).

Questions:

(a) Does the Banach space $H^1$ (defined above) admit a Schauder basis?

(b) Does $H^1$ admit an unconditional basis?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears to remain open. It is well known that the canonical basis $\{n^{-s}\}$ is unconditional in $H^p$ only when $p=2$, and surveys on Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series continue to list the existence of a (unconditional) basis for $H^1$ as an unresolved problem. Recent work (e.g., on translated Dirichlet series and on canonical-basis fundamental functions) addresses related but distinct settings rather than resolving the original question.

status_evidence.title: Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series and their operators: a survey
status_evidence.snippet: The introduction of H^p spaces raises some delicate problems, all of which are not solved.
status_evidence.claim: Survey indicates basis questions for H^p (p≠2) remain delicate and unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Hardy space of translated Dirichlet series (arXiv:2003.04041)
status_evidence.snippet: The Dirichlet monomials {n^{-s}} form an unconditional Schauder basis of the Hardy space of translated Dirichlet series H_+.
status_evidence.claim: Unconditional basis property is established for a modified (translated) Hardy space, not for the original H^1.
